question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-5^x-3?$
question.explanation:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • We take the curve $y=5^x.$
  • Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-5^x.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$
  • Then, vertically shift it by $3$ units down to give $y=-5^x-3.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(0,-4)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-3.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^{x}+4?$
question.explanation:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • We take the curve $y=\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^{x}.$
  • Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$
  • Then, vertically shift it by $4$ units up to give $y=-\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^{x}+4.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(0,3)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=4.$
